name: Pau Branco mine: Dique Lisa overflow onto BR-040

name: Brumadinho: Córrego do Feijão dam collapse
place: Córrego do Feijão mine, Brumadinho, Minas Gerais; mud reached the Paraopeba river
deaths: 270 (most common count); 272 counting two unborn babies. Other counts: 265 dead plus 5 missing (CUT); 258 dead plus 11 missing (Outras Palavras). 6 still missing in Jan 2022.
affected: About 1,400 victims from Brumadinho and Mário Campos are suing TÜV SÜD AG in Munich for about R$ 3.2 billion (hearings set for 26-28 May 2026; outcome not found).

Criminal: 16 people (11 Vale, 5 TÜV SÜD) and two companies charged; case moved to federal court. In April 2026 the STJ reinstated the case against ex-CEO Fabio Schvartsman. No conviction yet. CVM cleared Schvartsman in Dec 2024 and fined ex-director Poppinga R$ 27 million (regulatory, not criminal).
summary: The Córrego do Feijão dam collapsed on 25 Jan 2019 and killed about 270 people. Vale and TÜV SÜD blame each other. Vale signed a R$ 37.68 billion deal in 2021, but seven years on there is no criminal conviction.

operator: Illegal gold miners (garimpeiros), plus licensed garimpo permits (PLGs) held by cooperatives

name: Mariana / Rio Doce: Fundão tailings dam collapse
place: Bento Rodrigues, Mariana, Minas Gerais; mud reached Barra Longa, the Rio Doce and Espírito Santo (Linhares)
operator: Samarco (joint venture of Vale and BHP Billiton)
linked_transfer: Vale, a Samarco co-owner, was sold in the Vale privatization auction, 6 May 1997
deaths: 19 (plus one forced miscarriage in one source infobox)
affected: Communities along the Rio Doce. A 2019 study found metals in house dust in Mariana and Barra Longa above legal limits. A survey of 289 families in Barra Longa (576 people) found 35% said health worsened (self-reported).
damage: Mud down the Rio Doce to the sea. Tailings volume is unsettled: about 62 million m3 released (PT Wikipedia), 40 million (Intercept via search), or 30 to 44.5 million in the original notes. Cadmium in soil and sediment up to 17 times the reference value in Mariana and Barra Longa.
legal_outcome: Civil: 2024 repactuação worth R$ 170 billion, signed 25 Oct 2024 and homologated by the STF on 6 Nov 2024. Criminal: first-instance acquittal (Nov 2024, Ponte Nova, per search summary). In Sept 2026 the TRF-6 2nd Panel unanimously overturned it in part and convicted Samarco and three former managers. Acquittals kept for Vale, BHP Billiton Brasil, VOGBR and three individuals. Appeals possible; MPF is assessing.
summary: The Fundão dam, run by Samarco, collapsed on 5 Nov 2015 and killed 19 people. Mud reached the Rio Doce and the sea. A R$ 170 billion settlement was approved in 2024. In 2026 a court convicted Samarco and three former managers, while Vale and BHP stayed acquitted.

summary: A tailings dam at the Herculano mine collapsed on 10 Sept 2014 and killed three workers. The company blamed a rare geological event. Directors were sent to a jury trial in 2022, and no verdict was found.

name: Kinross gold mine, Paracatu: tailings dams and arsenic
place: Paracatu, Minas Gerais; Rio Paracatu
affected: Quilombolas have filed civil actions (Correio Braziliense, Sept 2025); the R$ 1 billion claim amount could not be confirmed. A Ministry of Science study found low arsenic in 95% of 1,000 people tested, but an MP report says tests were redone after equipment failure.
damage: Arsenic and heavy metals found in soil, water and urine (MPF and CETEM experts). Kinross says arsenic is natural and below WHO limits and denies using arsenic. Dams: Santo Antônio (built 1987, about 483 million m3) and Eustáquio (operating since 2010, about 750 million m3), about 1.2 billion m3 combined.
legal_outcome: MPMG civil action (2023) to stop tailings deposit at Santo Antônio and Eustáquio; first-instance rejection not found in the fact-check. Separate MPMG request to freeze R$ 5 million over siren misuse (unverified). MPF is negotiating a deal with Kinross for Machadinho, Amaros and São Domingos.
summary: Kinross runs one of Brazil's largest gold mines at Paracatu, with two very large tailings dams. Prosecutors and quilombola communities raise arsenic and dam-safety concerns. Kinross says arsenic is natural and below limits.

name: Estrada de Ferro Carajás and the Carajás corridor

affected: The line crosses over 100 communities in 27 municipalities, including Indigenous lands and quilombola territories. 14 houses damaged in Auzilândia, 48 under evaluation; about 200 families in risk areas in Marabá (Civil Defence).

legal_outcome: Vale was behind more than 170 people being targeted in at least 57 civil and criminal actions from 2013 to Oct 2017. Vale says it acts when its possession is threatened.
summary: The Carajás railway carries ore from the mines to the coast and cuts through over 100 communities. Dozens of people have died in train accidents since 2010. Vale also sued many residents, who say they are blocked from crossings.

name: Caldas uranium mine and tailings, Poços de Caldas
place: Caldas / Poços de Caldas, Minas Gerais; Córrego Consulta
affected: ANM estimates up to 500 people in a rupture.
damage: BAR dam holds about 2.5 million m3 of uranium tailings (0.70% grade). ANM rates rupture impact as 'muito significativo agravado'; seepage seen on the downstream face in a 2023 ANM inspection. CNEN admitted seepage and an acid drainage plume reaching Córrego Consulta; INB denied soil or water contamination in 2017.
legal_outcome: Dam at emergency level 1; independent auditors did not certify stability in early Oct 2023. MPF has followed it since 2019 and recommends an emergency plan. It cannot be embargoed because the material has nowhere to go (CNEN). Responsibility moved from CNEN to ANM under Law 14.514 (Dec 2022). No decommissioning plan in the article.
summary: INB's Caldas uranium mine, active 1980-1995, left a dam with about 2.5 million m3 of tailings. The dam is at emergency level 1 and has no stability certificate. INB says level 1 means no imminent rupture risk.
